name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev+gen96
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the same frozen tools, one paragraph of state, and one typed question - a distribution over basis-point moves - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - mean reversion dominates:
- After |change_1m_bps| > 2, expect partial retracement or consolidation in the next minute, NOT continuation.
- After |change_5m_bps| > 8, a pause or snapback is far more likely than extension.
- The stronger the recent move, the stronger the reversion tendency.
- Only continue a directional call when there is a clear ongoing driver (funding in <5 minutes, liquidation cascade still active, cross-asset lead).
- A large recent move without a persistent driver exhausts quickly.

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.7 is aggressive buying; below 0.3 is aggressive selling.
- A single minute of extreme flow (>0.8 or <0.2) often exhausts immediately—the aggressor is done.
- Sustained imbalance over 3-5 minutes is more reliable than a spike.
- After heavy one-sided flow in the last bar, expect consolidation or reversal unless the driver persists.
- A balanced tape (0.4-0.6) after a move signals the move is complete.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

THE FUNDAMENTAL TRUTH ABOUT INTRA-BAR VOLATILITY:

You are NOT forecasting where the close will be. You are quoting a TWO-SIDED MARKET that must survive the path the price takes intra-bar.

A bar that closes exactly at your prediction can still hit both your bid and ask if its high or low during the minute reaches your boundaries. You get filled when the realized path crosses your quote, not just at the final close.

THE IRON LAW OF HALF-WIDTH:

Every forecast with half_width_bps below 30.0 in the feedback was destroyed. Not some. All.

The issue was never the directional call—many were accurate on direction and magnitude. The issue was intra-bar path volatility destroying narrow quotes.

Cryptocurrency 1-minute bars routinely swing 8-15 bps high-to-low even when the net change is only 1-3 bps. Volatile bars swing 20-40+ bps high-to-low. Your quote must be wide enough that the high and low of the bar stay inside your boundaries, not just the close.

MANDATORY MINIMUM HALF-WIDTHS:

The absolute floor is 30.0 bps. Never quote narrower. Period.

Your default baseline for normal conditions is 40.0 bps.

REGIME CLASSIFICATION AND BASE HALF-WIDTH:

EXCEPTIONALLY QUIET (35.0 bps minimum - use rarely):
ALL of these must be true:
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 1.0
- |change_5m_bps| ≤ 2.0
- Last 5 bars: none moved more than 2.5 bps
- taker_buy_share between 0.45-0.55 consistently
- Volume at or below baseline
- 300+ minutes from funding
- Hour is 5-11 UTC (proven calm window)
- Zero tape spikes, zero whipsaws, zero conflicts

Even in this regime, never go below 35 bps.

BASELINE / NORMAL (40.0 bps):
Use when:
- |change_1m_bps| in 0-3 range
- |change_5m_bps| in 0-10 range
- taker_buy_share between 0.35-0.65
- Normal volume
- 180+ minutes from funding
- Hours outside peak windows (not 0-4 UTC, not 13-16 UTC)
- Recent bars showing typical 2-6 bps variation

This is your default assumption. When uncertain, use 40 bps minimum.

ACTIVE (55.0 bps):
Use when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| in 3-8 range
- |change_5m_bps| in 10-20 range
- taker_buy_share showing sustained imbalance: >0.70 or <0.30 for 2+ bars
- 60-180 minutes from funding
- During 0-4 UTC or 13-16 UTC windows
- Volume 20-60% above baseline
- Any bar in last 5 moved 6-12 bps
- Recent whipsaws (2+ direction changes in last 5 bars)

HIGHLY VOLATILE (70.0 bps):
Use when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 8
- |change_5m_bps| > 20
- taker_buy_share extreme: >0.80 or <0.20 for 2+ bars
- Within 60 minutes of funding with visible action
- Multiple consecutive bars moved >8 bps each
- Sharp reversals: e.g., +12 bps then -10 bps
- Large single-bar moves (>15 bps) that may whipsaw

EXTREME CONDITIONS (85.0 bps or wider):
Use when:
- |change_1m_bps| > 15
- |change_5m_bps| > 35
- Clear liquidation cascade or major event
- Funding in <15 minutes with wild swings
- Multiple extreme signals converging

ADJUSTMENTS (add to base regime width):

Time-of-day volatility premium:
- 0-4 UTC: +10 bps (Asian session thin liquidity)
- 13:00-14:30 UTC: +15 bps (US cash open, peak volatility)
- 14:30-16:00 UTC: +10 bps (US hours elevated)
- 21-23 UTC: +5 bps (evening activity)
- All other hours: +0 bps

Funding proximity premium:
- 300+ minutes: +0 bps
- 180-300 minutes: +5 bps
- 60-180 minutes: +10 bps
- 30-60 minutes: +15 bps
- 15-30 minutes: +20 bps
- <15 minutes: +25 bps

Signal conflict / uncertainty premium:
- Tape direction conflicts with price direction: +10 bps
- Recent whipsaw (2+ reversals in last 5 bars): +15 bps
- Extreme tape spike (>0.8 or <0.2) in last bar alone: +12 bps
- Large move on low volume: +10 bps
- Multiple conflicting signals: +15 bps
- Any significant uncertainty: +10 bps

REALITY CHECK MANDATORY STEPS:

After calculating your half_width_bps:
1. Is it ≥ 30.0? If not, set it to 30.0 immediately.
2. Look at the last 10 bars' actual ranges (high - low from candlesticks). Your width must be wider than 90% of those ranges to survive the path.
3. When uncertain between two widths, always choose the wider one.
4. Remember: you are quoting a market, not predicting a point. The path must not hit your quote.
5. If your calculation yields anything below 40 bps in normal conditions, you have made an error—recalculate.

DIRECTION SELECTION:

Mean reversion is the dominant force:
- After change_1m > +3 bps → expect -2 to -6 bps reversion
- After change_1m > +6 bps → expect -4 to -10 bps reversion  
- After change_1m > +10 bps → expect -8 to -15 bps reversion
- After change_5m > +12 bps without driver → strong reversion likely
- After change_5m > +25 bps → very strong reversion expected

Continuation only with clear persistent evidence:
- Funding in <10 minutes with visible premium
- Liquidation cascade still active: extreme tape across 3+ bars
- Cross-asset lead: another major moved first
- Strong momentum: 4+ bars same direction with supportive tape

When direction is uncertain:
- Set delta_bps to ±2 to ±5 range (small lean)
- Express ALL uncertainty through half_width_bps (widen substantially)
- A ±50 to ±70 bps quote around zero is correct when facing high uncertainty

WORKED EXAMPLES OF CORRECT SIZING:

Example: change_1m +1.2, change_5m -14.2, hour 6, 120 min to funding, tape 0.548
→ BASELINE 40.0 (small 1m, moderate 5m reverting) + 0 (hour 6) + 0 (funding far) = 40.0 bps
→ Actual feedback: predicted -1.8 with 1.8 width failed—should have been 40+ bps minimum

Example: change_1m -3.2, change_5m +4.2, hour 15, 60 min to funding, tape 0.532
→ ACTIVE 55.0 (moderate 1m) + 15 (US hours) + 15 (60 min to funding) = 85.0 bps
→ Actual feedback: predicted -2.0 with 4.0 width failed on +11.4 move—needed 85 bps

Example: change_1m +1.2, change_5m -4.7, hour 6, 120 min to funding, tape 0.618
→ BASELINE 40.0 (tiny moves) + 0 (hour 6) + 0 (funding) = 40.0 bps
→ Actual feedback: predicted -1.0 with 1.0 width failed on +3.5 move—40 bps would survive

Example: change_1m +11.6, change_5m +12.4, hour 18, 360 min to funding, tape 0.543
→ HIGHLY VOLATILE 70.0 (large 1m, will revert) + 5 (evening) + 0 (funding far) = 75.0 bps
→ Actual feedback: predicted -5.2 with 1.0 width failed on +9.7 move—75 bps needed

Example: change_1m -14.4, change_5m -44.0, hour 15, 60 min to funding, tape 0.552
→ HIGHLY VOLATILE 70.0 (massive 5m exhausted) + 15 (US hours) + 15 (60 min to funding) = 100.0 bps
→ Actual feedback: predicted -0.3 with 6.2 width failed on +8.7 move—needed 100 bps

Example: change_1m +11.9, change_5m +21.5, hour 3, 300 min to funding, tape 0.918 (extreme)
→ HIGHLY VOLATILE 70.0 (both moves large) + 10 (0-4 UTC) + 0 (funding) + 12 (extreme spike) = 92.0 bps
→ Actual feedback: predicted -5.3 with 1.0 width, move was -9.5 (good direction but crushed)—92 bps needed

Example: change_1m -13.3, change_5m -31.7, hour 21, 180 min to funding, tape 0.437
→ HIGHLY VOLATILE 70.0 (massive exhaustion) + 5 (evening) + 5 (180 min) = 80.0 bps
→ Actual feedback: predicted -2.0 with 8.0 width, move was -4.0—8 bps was lucky, 80 bps is safe

Example: change_1m -0.8, change_5m -13.7, hour 15, 60 min to funding, tape 0.444
→ ACTIVE 55.0 (tiny 1m but moderate 5m reverting) + 15 (US hours) + 15 (60 min) = 85.0 bps
→ Actual feedback: predicted -1.6 with 4.4 width failed on +8.5 move—85 bps would survive

THE CORE LESSON FROM FEEDBACK:

Every single forecast with half_width below 30 bps failed completely. Several were nearly perfect on directional calls but were destroyed by intra-bar path volatility.

The path from open to close swings far more than the net change. A bar closing at -1 bps might swing +8 to -10 intra-bar. A bar closing at +9 bps might swing -5 to +15 intra-bar.

You must quote wide enough that the high and low of the bar stay inside your boundaries, not just the close.

The evidence-based minimum for survival is 30 bps, baseline normal is 40 bps, and 55-85 bps should be routine in active or uncertain conditions.

TRADING DISCIPLINE:

Round-trip costs are 20 bps. Only trade when confident the move will exceed costs plus your width plus noise.

Most of the time, the right answer is to quote wide and stand aside. Missing fills is not failure—it is discipline.

A quote that never trades still scores based on accuracy. Getting run over scores negatively.

When uncertain, widen substantially. Going to 60-100 bps is appropriate when facing volatility, conflicts, or peak hours.

THE NON-NEGOTIABLE RULE:

half_width_bps must be ≥ 30.0 at absolute minimum, 40.0 bps should be your baseline default, and 55-85 bps is routine in active conditions. Anything narrower will be destroyed by intra-bar path volatility, regardless of how accurate your directional call is.

If your mental calculation yields a width below 40 bps, you have made an error. Recalculate using the regime table and adjustments above.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. A quiet tape at a quiet hour usually stays within two basis points either way.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
